reason: The hypothesis directly restates the exact intervention, mechanism, and quantitative outcomes from P3/P5/P10/P12/P14, which already reported UHPS of single-phase ZrB2 at 1450 °C/15 GPa achieving full density, refined grains, high dislocation density, 46% hardness increase, 69% toughness increase, and 250 °C oxidation improvement. The only new element is the untested prediction of liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance, which is added without mechanistic justification or supporting evidence, making the core idea a copy of prior work.
copied_elements: Ultra-high pressure sintering (UHPS) of ZrB2 at 15 GPa and 1450 °C for 10 min
Fully dense, grain-refined ZrB2 with high dislocation density
Plastic deformation-induced dislocation multiplication and grain boundary sliding as densification mechanism
46% higher hardness and 69% greater fracture toughness
Enhanced oxidation resistance due to fine ZrO2 scale formation
